1	# INDEX_RULES.md — Global Rules & Doc Routing
2	
3	**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/agents-config/blob/main/INDEX_RULES.md>
4	
5	**TLDR:** Read this compact contract at task start, then read only the detailed rule sections whose triggers apply. All agents use the same policy; client-specific loading differs.
6	
7	## How to load these rules
8	
9	Refresh `~/agents-config` with `git -C ~/agents-config pull --ff-only` at each new non-trivial task and after an hour; preserve dirty/concurrent work and use the local copy if offline. Reread this index and relevant changed rules. When editing agents-config in an isolated checkout, use that checkout's index and detail files after refreshing the home checkout.
10	
11	All Hard Rule **Details** links and matching Trigger Rule/Guideline links are mandatory routing: **before the action they govern, read that detail section and its applicable workflow**, including secret overrides, spending and review decisions. Do not read every topic file. Rule numbers are stable; paths below resolve beneath `~/agents-config/` (or the active agents-config checkout). If files are unavailable locally, fetch the same path under `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brando90/agents-config/main/`. A Markdown link is a reading instruction, not proof the client loaded it. Never eagerly import this index or the detail collection into an entry file; read them as task files.
12	
13	Hard rules govern conflicts with older wording in a triggered procedure. Explicit user instructions and platform/tool constraints retain their normal precedence. The SNAP pre-approval in Trigger Rule 51 is scoped to authorized work and existing budgets. Detail pages retain the procedures, examples and exceptions; the catalog is optional lookup.
14	
15	## Hard Rules (every response, never skip)
16	
17	1. **Protect secrets.** Never commit credentials; inspect the exact staged diff and filenames before committing or pushing. Do not print secret values. Stop on a suspected leak and rotate exposed credentials; references/env vars replace embedded secrets. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-1)
18	
19	2. **Sync, then verify before pushing.** `git fetch` first; if upstream moved, rebase and re-test; never force-push a shared branch. Never fabricate unavailable source content; mark it unresolved. Inspect the diff and run the relevant deterministic checks. Report actual evidence and limitations, not an untested success claim. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-2)
20	
21	3. **Quality assurance (QA) is opt-in.** Only a tier Brando explicitly requests or sets for this work in a runbook, `[qa]`/`[light-qa]`/`[mega-qa]` commit tag or environment flag starts a model reviewer. Hooks, project files and older “QA required” text are not opt-in. “Do QA”/“light QA” means one opposite-company round; apply findings and verify without automatic re-review. Mega QA follows Trigger Rule 10. Hooks cannot impose unsolicited QA; do not mention QA when unrequested. Benchmark-reference acceptance (43) remains separate. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-3)
22	
23	4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)
24	
25	5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)
26	
27	6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)
28	
29	7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)
30	
31	8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)
32	
33	9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)
34	
35	10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)
36	
37	11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)
38	
39	## Trigger Rules (mandatory when triggered)
40	
41	Read the linked rule **before** its action. Multiple rows may apply. Stanford Network Analysis Project (SNAP) is the remote cluster; a pull request (PR) is a proposed Git change. PDF means Portable Document Format.

121	| [83](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-83) | Research/startup/eval with unknown need → ask if it should exist; run the quickest de-risking test locally, email results, write repo MD files; endpoints/logins in parallel; once it covers the main risk, push velocity. |
122	| [84](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-84) | Run/score/report vb-priv (or new VeriBench runs) → int_ref is the most important metric: run it once, save per-task results, derive int from it, lead updates with it. |
123	| [85](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-85) | Write/edit/review ML research text (papers, reports, research Docs, updates) → load `skills/scientific-terminology`: one term per concept, reuse exactly, no stylistic synonyms. |
124	| [86](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-86) | Claude app/claude.ai session start, Project change, new account sign-in, or Projects missing from the left → every Project of every account stays pinned in the sidebar; pin missing ones, run the session sync with `--all-accounts`, report counts; never wait to be asked. |
125	| [87](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-87) | Report results, hand off, or send/change anything in Brando's name → load `skills/assistant`: label what ran (Lean/reading, DT, harness, model), short results-first, no branches. |
126	
127	## Guidelines (best practices)
128	
129	- [14](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-14): Complete direct authorized requests; do not ask again for already-authorized actions.
130	- [15](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-15): Read only task-relevant referenced docs.
131	- [16](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-16): Keep index, README and paths accurate; mirror shared entry bodies; verify actual host instruction files and reload state.

136	- [21](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-21): Check `~/keys/` for credentials, model-provider keys included, before asking; keep values transient.
137	- [22](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-22): Let the Node version manager control its path; avoid hardcoded versioned PATH entries.
138	- [23](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-23): Authorized email: Brando's signed-in account (mail connector, else uutils SMTP); BCC three inboxes, sender and To included; visible CC only on request; `drafted with <agent>` sign-off; “send” means send.
139	- [24](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-24): Paper PDFs follow mandatory Rule 35.
140	- [25](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-25): VeriBench/VB private: >0.98 saturated; ≤0.9 good, ≤0.5 great, 0 best. "Harsh metric", N tasks, ASCII, harness. vb-priv: SYNC.md. Any metric ≥~0.98: solved (heuristic). [Set names](workflows/vb-sets.md).

# INDEX_RULES.md — Global Rules & Doc Routing

**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/agents-config/blob/main/INDEX_RULES.md>

**TLDR:** Read this compact contract at task start, then read only the detailed rule sections whose triggers apply. All agents use the same policy; client-specific loading differs.

## How to load these rules

Refresh `~/agents-config` with `git -C ~/agents-config pull --ff-only` at each new non-trivial task and after an hour; preserve dirty/concurrent work and use the local copy if offline. Reread this index and relevant changed rules. When editing agents-config in an isolated checkout, use that checkout's index and detail files after refreshing the home checkout.

All Hard Rule **Details** links and matching Trigger Rule/Guideline links are mandatory routing: **before the action they govern, read that detail section and its applicable workflow**, including secret overrides, spending and review decisions. Do not read every topic file. Rule numbers are stable; paths below resolve beneath `~/agents-config/` (or the active agents-config checkout). If files are unavailable locally, fetch the same path under `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brando90/agents-config/main/`. A Markdown link is a reading instruction, not proof the client loaded it. Never eagerly import this index or the detail collection into an entry file; read them as task files.

Hard rules govern conflicts with older wording in a triggered procedure. Explicit user instructions and platform/tool constraints retain their normal precedence. The SNAP pre-approval in Trigger Rule 51 is scoped to authorized work and existing budgets. Detail pages retain the procedures, examples and exceptions; the catalog is optional lookup.

## Hard Rules (every response, never skip)

1. **Protect secrets.** Never commit credentials; inspect the exact staged diff and filenames before committing or pushing. Do not print secret values. Stop on a suspected leak and rotate exposed credentials; references/env vars replace embedded secrets. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-1)

2. **Sync, then verify before pushing.** `git fetch` first; if upstream moved, rebase and re-test; never force-push a shared branch. Never fabricate unavailable source content; mark it unresolved. Inspect the diff and run the relevant deterministic checks. Report actual evidence and limitations, not an untested success claim. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-2)

3. **Quality assurance (QA) is opt-in.** Only a tier Brando explicitly requests or sets for this work in a runbook, `[qa]`/`[light-qa]`/`[mega-qa]` commit tag or environment flag starts a model reviewer. Hooks, project files and older “QA required” text are not opt-in. “Do QA”/“light QA” means one opposite-company round; apply findings and verify without automatic re-review. Mega QA follows Trigger Rule 10. Hooks cannot impose unsolicited QA; do not mention QA when unrequested. Benchmark-reference acceptance (43) remains separate. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-3)

4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)

5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)

6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)

7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)

8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)

9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)

10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)

11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)

## Trigger Rules (mandatory when triggered)

Read the linked rule **before** its action. Multiple rows may apply. Stanford Network Analysis Project (SNAP) is the remote cluster; a pull request (PR) is a proposed Git change. PDF means Portable Document Format.

| Rule | When → required action |
|---|---|
| [6](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-6) | Edit agents-config → keep shared entries/routes consistent; reread, verify, commit and push the owned change. |
| [7](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-7) | Create a PR → concise Summary and Test plan, relevant report/doc links; no unsolicited dashboard. |
| [8](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-8) | Checks and requested review pass → commit/push; unresolved critical findings or failed review block landing. |
| [9](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-9) | Launch graphics-processor work → estimate resources, assign devices, respect allocation approval/SNAP pre-approval, verify and clean up. |
| [10](rules/safety-and-models.md#trigger-rule-10) | Explicit Mega QA → three sequential review stages; preserve required model/family gates. |
| [11](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-11) | Requested QA passes and ultimate-utils reaches master → version, build and publish the package. |
| [12](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-12) | New session/background work → inspect existing workers; clean only >24-hour processes confirmed idle. |
| [13](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-13) | Research paper work or validity question → load research-writing guide; preserve evidence and source format. |
| [14](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-14) | New verified results, any agent/duration → chat ping + email including brandojazz and brando.science; verify/deduplicate delivery. Confirm routine pushes in chat. Email a push receipt only on request. |
| [15](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-15) | Substantive question → answer in chat; email only when explicitly requested. |
| [16](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-16) | Create/edit documents or save knowledge → headers; Google companion for findings; separate dated daily audience decks; verify. |
| [17](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-17) | Authorized task → finish relevant end-to-end work, verification and authorized publication; no smoke-only stopping. |
| [18](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-18) | Appendix/results/polish-only branch → inspect scope and land; substantive claims keep authorization. |
| [19](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-19) | Create/finish checkouts, merge branches or write in `~` → one canonical project; remove temp copies, run the sweep; no `~` clutter. |
| [20](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-20) | Lean proof/type-check task → discover pinned toolchain and actually compile; report observed output. |
| [21](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-21) | Paper introduction → load introduction and general research-writing guides. |
| [22](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-22) | Paper abstract → load abstract and general guides; preserve structural source comments. |
| [23](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-23) | Reader-facing prose → omit internal course/lab planning jargon. |
| [24](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-24) | Reader outside a subfield → translate ambiguous jargon and explain concepts first. |
| [25](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-25) | Personal blog → load personal-blog guides and reference posts; lab blogs use their separate route. |
| [26](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-26) | Email → BCC three Brando inboxes, use visible CC only on request; no ratings emails to collaborators without his yes; signature; plain takeaway. |
| [27](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-27) | Chat answer → plain direct first sentence, never an opening `A (TLDR)`/TLDR label (only `TLDR-end`); explainer-doc Q&A → `**A (TLDR):**` line. |
| [28](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-28) | Attached image/transcription → preserve original and provenance in the canonical project/experiment location. |
| [29](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-29) | Exact “Q go” plus screenshots → numbered question packet, original images, issue, verification and publication; review still follows Hard Rule 3. |
| [30](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-30) | Conference poster → load poster/research guides, compile and inspect rendering. |
| [31](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-31) | Lab paper blog/roundup → load lab-blog guide; draft in paper repo and obtain coauthor sign-off before publication. |
| [32](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-32) | Paper/release X thread → load thread guide; verify lengths, supported numbers and privacy gates. |
| [33](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-33) | Paper/release LinkedIn post → load LinkedIn guide; preserve numbers, author/privacy policies and review delivery. |
| [34](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-34) | Browser/account/form task → finish forms/files/sign-in; act on clear approval replies (including "I read it") to the pending checkpoint; verify. |
| [35](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-35) | Semantic paper-source edit → compile and commit fresh PDFs beside active paper sources; verify build and references. |
| [36](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-36) | Handoff/reusable/scheduled prompt → use the appropriate summary format; selection advice stays outside, execution facts inside; preserve schedule settings. |
| [37](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-37) | Long/dispatched run → maintain and publish live canonical results.md from launch; Markdown record + Google findings (Rule 16); dashboards opt-in. |
| [38](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-38) | SNAP connection or dispatch → check the official gateway before Cisco/Duo escalation; automatic reconnect is allowed with one shared five-host cooldown/backoff (never flood it); run relevant health preflight; token-spending checks remain opt-in. |
| [39](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-39) | Start/continue/finish experiment → canonical setup-named home/index, colocated artifacts, results tables in git, frozen evidence, lifecycle; research repos: no branches, straight to `main`. |
| [40](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-40) | Commit slide deck → fresh PDF, applicable text sibling and hash manifest in the same commit. |
| [41](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-41) | End substantive replies with a ranked `[p N/10]` list; start 9-10 items without spending or rule violations. |
| [42](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-42) | Dispatch beyond short lookup → owned checkout, named persistent session, verified launch/live records and completion watch; an agent in a numbered/stale session renames it to `<client>-<project>-<role>-<task>`. |
| [43](rules/safety-and-models.md#trigger-rule-43) | Benchmark reference edit → strongest-tier Claude AND Codex acceptance for every landed change; preserve attribution. |
| [44](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-44) | Long run, account/context/turn limit, or session end in an experiment folder → durable timestamped `CKPT_<task>.md`; update only on events: edit the ≤30-line state block, append one dated log line, never rewrite; exact continuation, verified handoff. |
| [45](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-45) | Ongoing coordinator → stable uniquely identified master checkpoint linking owned workers, watches and next commands. |
| [46](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-46) | Remote publishable phase → PR, exact-revision checks, requested review, immediate merge, receipt, safe sync. |
| [47](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-47) | Question about another agent → read its task context; distinguish chat activity, schedule and actual execution/results. |
| [48](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-48) | Dispatch or account/provider/context/turn limit → inventory authorized existing accounts; bound/verify handoff; keep one writer and scientific limits. “ac-scheduler” → host watch, master check-in, authorized notifications. |
| [49](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-49) | Research root layout/tidy → four content buckets and root allowlist; inventory live consumers before moves. |
| [50](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-50) | Uncertain research/design → choose consequential uncertainty and cheapest valid test; record criterion before measuring. |
| [51](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-51) | Launch/resume/supervise any agent → verify effective full access/no routine approvals and first useful action; queued approval is not recovery; preserve task/platform/budget limits and exact SNAP pre-approval. |
| [52](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-52) | Board-visible job → run-bound fresh receipts, ordinary-code liveness and verified board row; separate coordinator and execution state. |
| [53](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-53) | Human-facing dates/new dated names → MM-DD-YYYY; preserve machine formats, existing names and frozen records. |
| [54](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-54) | Experiment → full folder name (first mention per section, each table row, summary). Paper no. → add title. |
| [55](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-55) | Run jobs → prefer remote compute; bounded local CPU fallback needs no approval; verify execution. |
| [56](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-56) | New day/planning/pasted task list → read weekly-notes source when available, compare latest section, disclose gaps; edit it only when Brando asks, additively. |
| [57](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-57), [74](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-74) | Would stall on scope, routing, approval or a click → decide (no-human route), record it; no self-made gates; to-dos only Brando's own. Grade next steps /10; do ≥9 now. |
| [58](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-58) | Capacity/tool gap → checkpoint and continue through eligible existing accounts/agents; one failed route is not all accounts exhausted. |
| [59](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-59) | Mac freeze/Chrome zombie leak → load diagnosis playbook and repair the responsible parent, preserving tripwire. |
| [60](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-60) | Technical explainer/teaching → use explainer style; paper prose uses its separate research style. |
| [61](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-61) | Solver/agent evaluation → freeze and finish full declared set within fixed budgets; retain every failed/missing cell and distinguish recovery. |
| [62](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-62) | Connector use, host setup, or unfamiliar/failing tool/service → read the connector cross-check and verified-host routes; investigate evidence, never fabricate missing content, recover and verify. |
| [63](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-63) | “Text me” → WhatsApp self-chat via quiet verified route; confirm sent state and surface human-only linking. |
| [64](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-64) | Explicit weekly update → newest-first project folder, complete post plus appendix/images; publish and return full post/path; keep sealed data sealed; sync knowledge under Rule 16; preserve his task-list text. |
| [65](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-65) | Open files for Brando in an editor → one call `cursor -n <project root> <files…>` (new window for that project); never `-r` or per-file open prompts. |
| [66](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-66) | Brando's AI meeting notes (Fathom link/ID, "get my notes") → verbatim transcript first, then summary and action items; script-written byte-exact copies with provenance in the named folder; never retype or reconstruct. |
| [67](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-67) | Brief a worker, write a prompt or describe what an agent may do → default to allowed; state only binding limits, no precautionary bans or reassurance. |
| [68](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-68) | Create or copy a Google Doc/Sheet/Slides/Drive file → share "Anyone with the link" at creation: Viewer by default, Editor when readers fill it in; restricted only for secrets, sealed or private data. |
| [69](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-69) | Dispatch or wait on a worker → watch for death too (`scripts/watch_worker.sh`: done, dead, credit/limit-blocked, idle, timeout); on failure recover at once on the next eligible account (Rule 58). |
| [70](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-70) | Launch or finish an experiment or long job (training/eval, cluster/background job, or >~15 min; never chat turns) → `[RUN START] <name>` then `[RUN DONE] <name>: <status>` email; recipient copies per Rule 26, deduplicate with Rule 14. |
| [71](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-71) | Session start, shared state, or need the assistant → `agent_sync.py check` the SYNC.md, name conflicts; read `[FROM-UB9]` in the repo's inbox issue (#68); ask with `[TO-UB9]` + email. |
| [72](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-72) | Launch/resume a Vals-paid run → one large experiment at a time across projects (`valk` gate); queue, estimate cost; only Brando overrides. |
| [75](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-75) | Run pending, capped or failed on one cluster → try every reachable cluster yourself on empty GPUs, free hardware, no Duo; release idle. |
| [73](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-73) | Desktop session pins → only active or awaiting-Brando sessions, dated title; unpin sessions when done (never Projects, Rule 86). |

| [81](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-81) | Verified work, any Brando repo → land on `origin/main` now; never park on a branch. |
| [80](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-80) | Launch/queue/size any GPU run, or free GPUs on mercury1/2 → use mercury as much as possible, whole node OK; empty GPUs only, never touch running jobs, shard big models over 4-5 A4000s, release when done. |
| [82](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-82) | Plan, run, score or report anything on public VeriBench → use the current release (`veribench@1.3`, 896 tasks, 10-28-2026); before each run `git ls-remote` veribench `main` and read its README release section; name the version beside every number. |
| [83](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-83) | Research/startup/eval with unknown need → ask if it should exist; run the quickest de-risking test locally, email results, write repo MD files; endpoints/logins in parallel; once it covers the main risk, push velocity. |

| [85](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-85) | Write/edit/review ML research text (papers, reports, research Docs, updates) → load `skills/scientific-terminology`: one term per concept, reuse exactly, no stylistic synonyms. |
| [86](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-86) | Claude app/claude.ai session start, Project change, new account sign-in, or Projects missing from the left → every Project of every account stays pinned in the sidebar; pin missing ones, run the session sync with `--all-accounts`, report counts; never wait to be asked. |
| [87](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-87) | Report results, hand off, or send/change anything in Brando's name → load `skills/assistant`: label what ran (Lean/reading, DT, harness, model), short results-first, no branches. |

## Guidelines (best practices)

- [14](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-14): Complete direct authorized requests; do not ask again for already-authorized actions.
- [15](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-15): Read only task-relevant referenced docs.
- [16](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-16): Keep index, README and paths accurate; mirror shared entry bodies; verify actual host instruction files and reload state.
- [17](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-17): Use anchored paths in prose and commands.
- [18](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-18): Use `ls -la` for configuration/credential directories.
- [19](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-19): Select experiment models/judges by capability, total cost and validation; preserve pins.
- [20](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-20): Messages/drafts as Brando use his concise first-person voice; email includes required routing/signature.

## Hard Rule 4

4. **TLDR at the end.** Every response must end with a `**TLDR-end:**` line — 1–2 sentences — written last, from the actual response content, so it reflects any conclusion that changed along the way. Do not open responses with a `**TLDR-start:**` line; Brando retired the opening TLDR on 2026-09-14. **Project tag:** prefix the TLDR with a square-bracket tag in the format `[proj: task]` — **project first**, then the current task; if there is no clear task yet, project only: `[proj]`. Use a concise/abbreviated project name (e.g. `vb` for veribench, `beyond-scale`) — e.g. `**TLDR-end:** [vb: leap-gemini-key] …` — so Brando can tell which project/conversation a response belongs to from the TLDR alone (he reviews many per day and otherwise cannot place them). Lean on the project as the anchor. Keep the whole tag short, and outside the 1–2 sentence budget.

   **Core-work reminder (Brando, 10-05-2026).** "Remind me what the most relevant/recent task you are doing (like important core experiment I mean, not small things like 'test arg', more like 'generating outputs with FMs for human judgements') … at the very least in the tldrs." The task part of the tag names the core experiment or deliverable the conversation is pursuing (what Brando would write in his weekly document), not the current micro-step; it changes only when the core work changes. A sub-step may follow `›`, for example `[vb: expt106 fake-human panel, leave-one-agent-out judge test › Argon smoke test]`. The TLDR's first clause restates that core work in plain words before the step's result, so a reader who sees only the TLDR knows which real experiment is running. Applies to all agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.). No exceptions.

   **Copy-ready weekly-update sentence (Brando, 09-24-2026).** For substantial research or experiment updates, open with one plain, self-contained sentence that Brando can paste directly into his weekly Google Doc: aim for one rendered line, two at most, matching the brevity of the approved example below. Keep the identifier first so truncated sidebars remain recognizable. Prefer the full sentence when supported; if a hard title limit applies, preserve identifier, distinguishing setup and status, and keep the full sentence in the task's first summary/checkpoint. Refresh the title when scope or material status changes; never imply the research goal is achieved merely because a run ended. Do not rename unrelated tasks speculatively. Agents own their title updates using their own evidence. Propagate rule changes with one brief notice at the next safe bound

**Compact results entries (Brando, 10-15-2026).** For a task-list result, weekly-update item or chat result summary, use **1–2 sentences plus two links**: state the finding with its decisive numbers and scope, then the material limitation or consequence. Finish with `Table:` and verified links labeled `.md` and `gdoc`. Keep full methods, uncertainty, factor tables and execution history in the linked reports. Do not expand a short result entry into the full-report template. If a requested link is unavailable, say so briefly; never invent one. See [the exact format](../workflows/statistics-reporting.md#compact-results-entry).

**Copy-ready collaborator message (Brando, 10-16-2026).** Whenever giving Brando research results, also include one **1–2 sentence message in Brando’s voice** that he can copy to Sanmi or the intended collaborator. Infer the audience from the conversation rather than always addressing Sanmi. ## What belongs here

| Folder | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| [rating_task_packet/](rating_task_packet/) | The task you edit and give to raters: instructions, scoring rubric, form guide, email draft, blank form and task files. |
| [ratings/](ratings/README.md) | Collected responses, named by person, with every live Google Sheet and matching comma-separated value (CSV) file linked. |
| [support/](support/README.md) | Coordinator records, provenance, scripts and tests. You do not need these to do your ratings. |

This README is the single collection overview: task links, people and completion status. Do not create separate index or status summaries at this level.

## Edit or prepare the task

- [START_HERE.md](rating_task_packet/START_HERE.md): short instructions and personal Sheet link.

[Prepared packets and exact team email previews](support/PREPARATION_11-09-2026.md#current-prepared-version--11-11-2026) are ready for review. **Before team dispatch:** finish Brando’s pilot, approve the revised email text, then explicitly say to send. tracked -= deleted
def is_tracked(rel):

def slugs(path):
    out = {}; res = set(); fence = False
    for l in open(path, encoding='utf-8'):
        if l.startswith('```'): fence = not fence
        if fence: continue
        m = re.match(r'^#{1,6}\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$', l)
        if not m: continue
        t = m.group(1)
        t = re.sub(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)', r'\1', t)
        t = re.sub(r'[`*]', '', t)
        s = re.sub(r'[^\w\- ]', '', t.lower()).replace(' ', '-')
        n = out.get(s, 0); out[s] = n + 1
        res.add(s if n == 0 else '%s-%d' % (s, n))
    return res
E = 'experiments/09_human_rating_collection'

bad = []; nlinks = 0
for f in files:

            if re.match(r'^(https?:|mailto:)', tgt): continue
            nlinks += 1
            p, _, frag = tgt.partition('#')
            dest = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(f), p)) if p else f
            ex = os.path.exists(dest)
            tr = is_tracked(dest) if ex else False
            anchor_ok = True
            if frag and ex and dest.endswith('.md'):

for o, f, ln, tgt, why in sorted(bad, key=lambda b: (not b[0], b[1], b[2])):

    print('anchor', a, 'in', f, '->', a in slugs(f))

tot_num = tot_na = 0
for f in sorted(os.listdir(E + '/ratings')):
    if not f.endswith('.csv'): continue
    rows = list(csv.reader(open(os.path.join(E, 'ratings', f), encoding='utf-8', newline='')))
    hdr_i = next((i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if 'rater_name' in r and 'rater_id' in r), None)
    if hdr_i is None: print('  NO HEADER', f, rows[:1]); continue
    hdr = rows[hdr_i]; body = [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in rows[hdr_i + 1:] if any(c.strip() for c in r)]
    sc = [b.get('final_score_0_5', '').strip() for b in body]
    num = sum(1 for s in sc if re.fullmatch(r'[0-5](\.\d+)?', s)); na = sum(1 for s in sc if s.upper() in ('N/A', 'NA')); blank = sum(1 for s in sc if s == '')
    other = len(sc) - num - na - blank
    tot_num += num; tot_na += na
    names = sorted(set(b.get('rater_name', '') for b in body)); ids = sorted(set(b.get('rater_id', '') for b in body))
    folders = sorted(set(b.get('task_folder', '') for b in body))
    print('  %-48s cols=%d rows=%d numeric=%d NA=%d blank=%d other=%d names=%s ids=%s folders=%d' % (f, len(hdr), len(body), num, na, blank, other, names, ids, len(folders)))
print('  TOTAL numeric=%d NA=%d' % (tot_num, tot_na))
print('\n### protected hashes')
ph = json.load(open('private/qa/human_rating_readme_11-11-2026/protected_hashes.json'))
mism = [p for p, h in ph.items() if not os.path.exists(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, 'rb').read()).hexdigest() != h]
print('  protected files:', len(ph), 'mismatches:', mism)
EOF

1	# Human-rating preparation — 11-09-2026
2	
3	**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/trustworthy-theorem-judges/blob/main/experiments/09_human_rating_collection/support/PREPARATION_11-09-2026.md>
4	
5	**TLDR:** The existing rating packet is available in this repository's private store. The preferred deadline is Friday, 11-13-2026; the final deadline is Sunday, 11-15-2026. Personal rating can start; collaborator dispatch remains a separate, explicitly approved action.
6	
7	## Current prepared version — 11-11-2026
8	
9	The current form has eleven columns, including estimated minutes, confidence, rationale (preferred but optional), and problem notes. All twelve live sheets and raw exports match it. All thirteen replacement packets preserve their original scientific file bytes and contain blank response forms. They are prepared, not sent; older deliveries remain immutable.
10	
11	- [Brando's six-file packet](../../../private/09_human_rating_collection/preparation_11-09-2026/packets/FormV5/VeriBench_warmup_A1_FormV5.zip) and [his sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VhlSsf8Fd_pD_hQySt4-Y3AHrj5e6Rd3kQFu6A59-8A/edit).
12	- [Current packet manifest](../../../private/09_human_rating_collection/preparation_11-09-2026/packets/FormV5/MANIFEST.json): recipient, route, item count, hashes and preserved scientific payload.
13	- [Eight exact team email previews](../../../private/09_human_rating_collection/preparation_11-09-2026/REVIEW_TEAM_EMAILS_FORM_V5.md) and [current dispatch queue](../../../private/09_human_rating_collection/preparation_11-09-2026/DISPATCH_QUEUE_FORM_V5.json).
14	- [Live-sheet and raw-context verification](sheet_exports/11-11-2026_final_form/README.md).
15	
16	Remaining before sending: Brando completes his pilot and approves the revised recipient-specific messages, then explicitly says to send. The current queue preserves eight existing recipients and their assignments; it does not assign the entire panel or recruit unconfirmed prospects. Rylan and Sri have ten assigned main files each, not all 125 rows visible in their sheets. More qualified raters/assignments are still needed for the 250-rating primary collection.
17	
18	The sections below record the original preparation and sending workflow. References to original attachments and the older REVIEW_TEAM_EMAILS.md describe historical drafts; use CURRENT_PREPARATION.json and the FormV5 review for the next dispatch.
19	
20	## Current collection
21	
22	**Coordination:** [Prepare human grading task](codex://threads/01a1a8f9-dcb7-7381-9368-91d6e51faffd) is the sole owner for this preparation and the practical human-rating judge. Follow the [consolidated ownership record](COORDINATION_11-09-2026.md); migration and historical methodology chats do not create separate dispatch owners.
23	
24	This is the inherited set-N collection: 25 Python tasks, five candidate files per task, and 125 candidate files. Its primary design calls for two qualified independent raters per candidate, or 50 folder assignments and 250 individual ratings. The coordinator's own ratings are an additional sensitivity panel, not replacements for those two ratings. These are design counts, not completed observations. This collection is separate from the larger prospective design in experiment 02.
25	
26	The active preparation record is `private/09_human_rating_collection/preparation_11-09-2026/README.md`. It contains the private roster, delivery queue, original attachments, source receipts, and proposed email bodies. The migration checkpoint beside this document tracks the broader move from VeriBench; this preparation record does not change that migration's files or ownership.
27	
28	## Verified preparation
29	
30	- The approved personal ZIP contains 25 folders and 125 candidates. Its bytes match the original delivery, and every extracted file matches the ZIP.

content.text:
The consolidation of `experiments/09_human_rating_collection` passes this light quality-assurance (QA) review: no critical or major issues, seven minor ones. Nothing in the new README is false, but a few guards and caveats from the deleted files were dropped or weakened.

Reviewer: Claude Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`), max effort, Claude Code; no files modified.

## What I checked

- **Patch scope:** the working tree equals `PATCH.diff`, only the 12 owned paths changed, and the untracked `rating_tensor_planning/` is still there.
- **Layout and mirror:** the experiment folder holds exactly `README.md`, `rating_task_packet/`, `ratings/`, `support/`; `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are byte-identical; `git diff --check` is clean.
- **Project check:** `python3 scripts/check_project.py` re-run gives 33 tests OK and left the worktree unchanged; all 29 protected packet/rating files match their recorded hashes.
- **Links:** every relative link and anchor in the patched files resolves, including the three new anchors (251 links in 40 files checked).
- **Counts:** the 12 raw comma-separated value (CSV) files have 11 columns each, 15 numeric ratings plus 3 `N/A`, and 0 main ratings; row counts are 6 and 125 as stated.
- **Assignments:** folders N17, N21 (Rylan) and N01, N23 (Sri) match the private delivered-assignment ledger.
- **Other consumers:** no script, JSON file or sister repository (`judges-dont-need-psychometrics-or-corr`, `cert-judge`, `veribench`, `agents-config`) references the deleted files.
- **Reading:** I compared both deleted files and the base README line by line against the new README and the import guide. Spelling was read by eye, since neither `aspell` nor `codespell` is installed.

## Findings (all minor, ranked)

Paths are relative to `experiments/09_human_rating_collection/` unless they start at the repository root.

1. **[p 7/10] The overview no longer says the 15 ratings are old data.**
   - `README.md:30` gives the count without "no new or revised ratings; all 15 match existing imports" (deleted `COMPLETION_STATUS.md:6`).
   - `README.md:47` turns "Re-exported copies are not new observations" (deleted `RATINGS_INDEX.md:31`) into "…re-exported copies are not completed main ratings", which is weaker.
   - The statement survives only in `support/IDENTITY_AND_IMPORT.md:67` and `ratings/SUMMARY.json`.
   - Fix: add the clause at line 30 and split line 47 into two sentences.

2. **[p 7/10] Slava's row blurs sent and unsent.**
   - `README.md:43` reads "Prepared CSV route; no returned CSV found in earlier scoped mail searches".
   - The missing return concerns his originally delivered warm-up. The linked form is the replacement, which `support/SLAVA_CSV_NAME_FIRST_11-11-2026.md:10` and deleted `RATINGS_INDEX.md:37` call prepared and unsent, with six blank rows.
   - Fix: "No returned CSV found for the original emailed warm-up; [replacement CSV form](…) prepared, unsent, six blank rows".

3. **[p 6/10] The entry line is Brando-specific but unlabeled.**
   - `README.md:3` links "your Google Sheet", which is Brando's warm-up Sheet, on a page listing ten people. `rating_task_packet/START_HERE.md:3` has the same link but adds "for Brando Miranda".
   - Fix: label it "Brando Miranda's warm-up Sheet", or link only `START_HERE.md`, which the project rule names as that link's home.
   - `README.md:9` ("The task you edit and give to raters") also drops "changes here are drafts until reviewed and packaged for delivery" (base `README.md:3`); restore that clause.

4. **[p 5/10] Three current statements still describe the old layout.**
   - Root `AGENTS.md:63` and `CLAUDE.md:63` say "Track the collected rating files, named index and completion status in Git directly under …", two lines below the new four-entry rule at line 61.
   - `support/COORDINATOR_README.md:33` uses the same phrase twice.
   - Its `## Files` tree (lines 55–73, stale before this patch) still shows `MIGRATION.json`, `PREPARATION_11-09-2026.md`, the checkpoint and `scripts/` at the top level.
   - Fix: reword to "rating files in `ratings/`, named completion table in the README", and replace the tree with the four entries or a pointer to `support/README.md`. Keep the two instruction files identical.

5. **[p 5/10] Root `README.md:71` has a dead anchor into this README.**
   - It links `experiments/09_human_rating_collection/README.md#current-delivery-status--11-09-2026`, which was already dead at base; the heading lives at `support/COORDINATOR_README.md:45`.
   - It is the "before sending" pointer and is outside the owned list.
   - Fix: retarget to `…/README.md#edit-or-prepare-the-task`, which now holds the dispatch gate, or to the coordinator heading.

6. **[p 4/10] Two caveats were dropped in the move.**
   - "This is collection evidence, not a fresh validation dataset" (deleted `COMPLETION_STATUS.md:37`) is in neither the README nor the new section at `support/IDENTITY_AND_IMPORT.md:60–72`. Add it after line 69.
   - "No reminders were sent" (deleted `COMPLETION_STATUS.md:25`) has no direct replacement. The nearest is `support/CKPT_human_rating_collection.md:11` ("Nothing has been sent in this revision"). Add a clause at `README.md:24` if you want it in the overview.

7. **[p 3/10] Polish.**
   - The README lacks the `**Doc link:**` and `**TLDR:**` lines that shared Rule 16 requires for rewritten documents; deleted `RATINGS_INDEX.md:6,8` had both.
   - `README.md:18` says "what to judge"; the project reserves "judge" for the model, so use "what to rate".
   - `README.md:22` says "eleven columns" and dropped "stored … internal keys hidden in Sheets" (base `README.md:14`).
   - `support/IDENTITY_AND_IMPORT.md:61–62` and `70–71` have doubled blank lines.
   - `.cursor/rules/project.mdc:29` and `:31` are two adjacent layout paragraphs; merge them.
   - `support/COORDINATOR_README.md:23` ("Start here … CSV files and Google Sheets") fits `../ratings/README.md` better, since line 30 already links the README table.

Not counted:
- Three dead links to the deleted files remain, by design, in two dated records: `support/NAME_FIRST_ROLLOUT_11-11-2026.md:13` and `support/sheet_exports/11-11-2026_all_raters_name_first/README.md:30`.
- `support/COORDINATOR_README.md:15` still says new forms use "the 18-column schema"; this predates the change.
- Both deleted files are on `origin/main` today, so any Google Doc or chat link to their GitHub pages will stop working after the push. I could not check those from here.

VERDICT: PASS
CRITICAL_ISSUES: 0
MAJOR_ISSUES: 0
MINOR_ISSUES: 7
